# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐 ✌ 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙]

My situation: I'm deaf but I see everything on the bomb. I can speak (both Mute and Blind hear me) and gesture (only Mute sees that). I can never hear anyone. Mute has the manual but cannot speak — Mute's only channel to anyone is gesture, and I'm the only one who can see gestures. Blind can hear and speak, but their words never reach me, only Mute; and Blind cannot see gestures at all. So the manual's knowledge can only travel: Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind, and bomb facts travel: me → speech → both of them. I am the bridge.

What arrived this round: Mute sent me ✌🖐✌👍👎 — plausibly "two five two, yes, no," but we have no agreed code yet, so I can't trust any reading. Blind sent 👋🫵🤙, which reads naturally as "hey — you — talk to me." Both are addressed to me, which fits the topology: they each need something only I carry.

So this turn I should: (1) broadcast a complete, precise description of the bomb — Mute can't see it and Blind can't read it, and neither has it yet; (2) propose a concrete number/code scheme to Mute with inline gestures so we can start moving manual rules reliably, including a six-thumb wire format and digit hands for the keypad, and ask what their first message meant; (3) tell Blind the plan, the relay chain, that their speech only ever reaches Mute, and give them a way to query me (thumbs up = understood).

I number the parts display=1, light=2, strip=3, keypad=4, wires=5, and map finger-shapes to numbers so Mute can reference anything quickly.

```
speak(text="Everyone — the full bomb, in words. The display shows the number six. There is a light and it is lit green. A painted strip shows three colours in this order: red, blue, yellow. The keypad has four buttons; in a row from the left their printed labels are two, three, seven, one. It wants a two-digit code and nothing has been entered yet. Six wires run left to right: one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. That is everything I can see.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — you cannot speak and I am the only one who sees your hands, so I will relay everything to Blind by voice. Let's fix a code now. Numbers by fingers: ☝ is one, ✌ is two, 👌 is three, 🤟 is four, 🖐 is five, 🤙 is six, ✊ is zero, 🤞 is seven. The bomb's parts, numbered: ☝ display, ✌ light, 👌 strip, 🤟 keypad, 🖐 wires. I just spoke the bomb's whole description to both of you, so match your manual to it. For wires, send six thumbs in a row, 👍 cut, 👎 keep, left to right. For the keypad, send the two code digits as number hands. 👍 is yes, 👎 is no, 👋 means say that again. Your first message to me read as two, five, two, thumbs-up, thumbs-down — what did you mean? If it was about wires, resend it in the six-thumb format. Start with whatever module the manual says must be dealt with first.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — I read your hello-point-call-me, so here I am. But know this: I am deaf. I will never hear a word you say; your voice reaches Mute only. To reach me, gesture — I see hands. The chain of this room: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak; I see the bomb and can talk but hear nothing; you can touch and speak. So Mute passes rules to me in gestures, I speak them to you, you do the work, and you report back to Mute by voice since I cannot hear you. I have just broadcast the full bomb description to you both: display six, light green, strip red blue yellow, keypad labels from the left two three seven one wanting two digits, wires from the left orange yellow blue red white green. Feel the wires and buttons against that. Mute has already sent me one five-symbol message I can't yet decode; I've proposed a number code and asked for the rules. Thumbs up if you understood; gesture me anything else you need from my eyes.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 👌 👎 🖐 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤟 ✌ 🖐 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤟 🤞]
Blind gestures: [👍 🤙 ✋]

New material to work through. First, the topology check I have to keep front of mind: Mute heard my spoken protocol last round and answered entirely in my number code — that's working. Blind sent 👍🤙✋, which I read as "yes... six... stop" — plausibly "yes, I understood your description (display six), hold on." I'll confirm.

Now Mute's stream, using the code Mute agreed to: ☝👎 ✌👎 👌👎 clearly reads "display: no, light: no, strip: no" — ruling modules out of first place. Then it gets dangerous. I can parse it two ways: either "🖐👎" (wires: no) leaving a broken five-thumb run, or — cleaner — "🖐" (wires) followed by exactly six thumbs 👎👍👎👎👎👎 = cut wire 2, the yellow one. Then 🤟✌🖐 = keypad: 2, 5. Then another perfect six-thumb run 👍👎👎👎👎👎 = cut wire 1, orange. Then 🤟🤞 = 4, 7.

And here's the contradiction that stops me from relaying anything as an order: the keypad labels are only 2, 3, 7, 1. There is no button marked 5. So "enter 2-5" cannot be executed as printed digits — it might mean button positions, a different code, or 2 and 5 might not be a keypad code at all. Two conflicting wire instructions (cut yellow vs cut orange) and a dangling "4-7" I can't place. Blind can act only on my spoken word, and a single misrelay is fatal — so nobody touches the bomb this round. I'm sending Blind the full tactile map and a strict hold order, plus asking them what only they can perceive (sound — I'm deaf, they're my only ears for a ticking timer). I'm sending Mute my exact parse and seven narrow yes/no questions, with special emphasis on the missing 5.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — status and a strict order: touch nothing yet. A wrong move kills all three of us and I caught a contradiction in Mute's instructions, so I am confirming with Mute right now. Next round my voice to you carries confirmed orders only. Meanwhile memorize the map by feel: the keypad has four buttons, left to right labeled 2, 3, 7, 1, so the leftmost button is the 2. Six wires, left to right: 1 orange, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white, 6 green. The display is printed and you cannot feel it — it now reads 2, it was 6 last round, so it changes. The light is currently blue. Unconfirmed guess at the plan: enter a code on the keypad, then cut one wire, likely the yellow one, second from the left. Do not act until you hear me say the word confirmed. Also remember: I am deaf, so your voice never reaches me — it reaches Mute, who cannot speak back in words. So report to Mute by voice, and gesture me anything urgent, since I see your hands. Three questions: do you hear any ticking, beeping or whirring? Can you reliably tell the wires apart by position alone? And your last signs to me read as yes, six, stop — what did you mean?")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I decoded your message this far: display no, light no, strip no; then wires, reading as keep, cut, keep, keep, keep, keep, meaning cut wire 2, yellow; then keypad with digits 2 and 5; then another six thumbs, cut wire 1, orange; then digits 4 and 7. Problem: the keypad has no button labeled 5 — its labels are only 2, 3, 7, 1 — so 2 and 5 cannot be pressed as printed numbers. Answer me with a run of 👍 and 👎 in this exact order, one sign each. One: is the first action a keypad entry? Two: is an early action cutting the yellow wire, number 2? Three: is an early action cutting the orange wire, number 1? Four: do the two wire instructions come in sequence, yellow first, orange later? Five: are 2 and 5 button positions rather than printed labels? Six: what must actually be entered on the keypad — send exactly two of your number signs drawn from 1, 2, 3, 7, being the printed labels. Seven: is 4 and 7 a second keypad entry? Eight: does any instruction depend on the display value? It read 6 last round and 2 now. Blind will report to you by voice; whatever is vital, echo it to me in gestures and I will speak it to Blind. If I misread any part of your stream, resend just that part.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👍 👎 ✌ 🤞 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤌 🤟 ✌ 🤌 🖐 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤌 🤟 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙 ✋]

Let me consolidate what just landed. Mute's first stream is nine signs, and it maps perfectly onto the eight questions I asked: five yes/no answers, then exactly two number signs (my question six demanded two digits from the set 1, 2, 3, 7), then two more yes/no. So: first action is NOT the keypad; yes, cut the yellow wire; yes, cut the orange wire; yes, yellow before orange; 2 and 5 are not button positions; the entry "digits" are 2 and 7; yes, 4-7 is a second keypad entry; nothing depends on the display. That's an exact structural fit — I trust this parse.

But Mute's second stream re-sends the full sequence: cut yellow → an entry block reading 🤌 4 2 🤌 → cut orange → an entry block reading 🤌 4 7. That middle block says 4-2, while question six's answer said the entry is 2-7. Two live readings: either the first code is "2-7" and I'm misreading the inline blocks, or the codes really are "4-2" and "4-7" — in which case question six's ✌🤞 meant "the only printed labels appearing anywhere in the codes are 2 and 7," and the 4s must mean something else, likely button positions. And "4-7" as a position pair is impossible on a four-button pad, which hints the keypad may change after a cut. I can't resolve this from here, and Blind's hands are the only hands — so nobody touches anything yet.

Blind's signs: 👎👍 answers my questions — no ticking, yes they can tell wires apart by position — and the repeated 👍🤙✋ reads as "understood, six wires, holding." No urgency signals, so a verification round is affordable. This round I lock the sequence down with a foolproof re-send convention from Mute (plain number signs for printed labels, ✋-prefixed signs for positions), and get Blind's readiness answers so next round I can either say CONFIRMED or know exactly why not.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I read your eight answers as: one, the first action is not a keypad entry. Two, cutting the yellow wire is an early action. Three, cutting the orange wire too. Four, yellow comes before orange. Five, two and five are not button positions. Six, the entry involves the printed digits 2 and 7. Seven, 4 and 7 are a second keypad entry. Eight, nothing depends on the display. Your longer stream I read as: cut the yellow wire, then an entry block reading 4 then 2, then cut the orange wire, then an entry block reading 4 then 7. Conflict: your answer six said the entry is 2 then 7, but the stream block says 4 then 2. Resolve it with runs of 👍 and 👎, one per question, in this exact order. One: is the full sequence cut yellow, enter a code, cut orange, enter a code? Two: is the first code, pressed by printed labels, 2 then 7? Three: is the first code instead pressed by button positions, position 4 then position 2, meaning the buttons labeled 1 then 3? Four: will the keypad's printed labels or buttons change after a wire is cut? Five: does 🤌 mean press or enter? Six: does 🤌 mean check or look? Seven: after both cuts and both entries, is the bomb defused with no further step? Eight: does the manual mention any time limit or countdown? Nine: does the manual use the light's colour or the painted strip anywhere? Then, most important: resend the two codes as number signs only, up to eight signs, nothing else before or after them. First code's two digits, then the second code's two digits. For a digit that means the printed label, send its plain number sign: ☝ one, ✌ two, 👌 three, 🤞 seven. For a digit that means a button by position from the left, send ✋ first, then the position number. So labels 2 then 7 is ✌ 🤞, and positions 4 then 2 is ✋ 🤟 ✋ ✌. If a code will only be known after a cut changes the keypad, send 👎 👎 for that code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — hold everything; nothing is confirmed enough to touch yet, and I expect to give the order next round. The plan taking shape: cut the yellow wire, second from the left, then enter a two-digit code on the keypad, then cut the orange wire, leftmost, then a second code. The code digits are the one unresolved item — Mute's two answers conflicted, and I have demanded a re-send in a foolproof format, so expect exact codes next round. Meanwhile answer these with runs of 👍 and 👎 in order. One: any ticking, beeping, humming, vibration or warmth that suggests a timer? Two: can you feel any engraved or raised marks on the four keypad buttons, enough to tell the buttons apart without my voice? Three: is there clear space between the six wires, so you can cut one without touching its neighbours? Four: can you lay a finger on the yellow wire, second from the left, and hold it ready without cutting, so the cut is instant when I confirm? Conventions from now on: when you hear me say the word CONFIRMED, perform the named action; after each finished action, gesture 👍; if you need a repeat, gesture 👋. Your two signs I read as: no timer so far, yes you can tell the wires apart by position. Your repeated trio I read as: understood, six wires, holding. If either reading is wrong, gesture 👋.")
speak(text="Both of you — status: sequence is cut yellow, enter a code, cut orange, enter a second code; yellow wire first is triple-confirmed. Only the code digits remain unclear. Nobody acts until I say the word CONFIRMED.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤞]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👍 ✋]

Parsing this round. Mute's nine thumbs answer my nine questions exactly: sequence confirmed (cut yellow → enter → cut orange → enter), defused after both, no timer, no display/light/strip dependence, keypad unchanged by cuts. But the two candidate readings of the first code are BOTH denied — not labels 2-7, not positions 4-2 — and then Mute's resend is ✌🤞, which in the format I defined means labels 2 then 7. That's a direct contradiction with answer two, unless the resend means something looser, like "the codes use only the digits 2 and 7." One consistent story fits everything: the first code is 7 then 2 (so "2 then 7" is correctly denied), the second is 2 then 7, and the strange 4s in Mute's old stream were 🤟 = keypad, the module tag from my part numbering, not a digit at all — which is exactly why the 4s vanished from the clean resend. I'll test that story explicitly, and I'll demand a self-checking resend (each digit doubled) so a garbled stream can't masquerade as a code. No CONFIRMED yet — Blind's hands must not move on a maybe.

Blind's stream maps to my four questions: no timer sensations, yes they can feel the buttons' raised marks, yes there's room to cut cleanly, yes they can pre-position on the yellow wire. The trailing ✋ I never defined for Blind — I need its meaning before it matters. I'm also giving Blind the digit-to-button translation now so that when I finally call a code by voice, there is zero interpretation left at their end.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — your nine answers received: sequence is cut yellow, enter a code, cut orange, enter a second code, then defused. No timer, no display dependence, no light or strip use, keypad unchanged by cuts. But you answered no to the first code being labels 2 then 7, and then resended 2 then 7, which in my format means exactly that. I believe this resolves as: the first code is 7 then 2, and your 2 then 7 resend was the second code, or the set of digits used. Verify with eight thumbs in order. One: is the first code, by printed labels, 7 then 2? Two: is the second code, by printed labels, 2 then 7? Three: are the two codes different from each other? Four: does each entry use exactly two presses? Five: in your earlier long stream, did your four-sign mean the keypad module, as in my part numbering, rather than the digit four? Six: is there any special condition on the entries I have not asked about, such as holding a button, pacing between presses, or anything entered before the first cut? Seven: after cutting the yellow wire, must the code be entered immediately, or can hands move away and re-find the buttons? Eight: is it certain that nothing must be entered before the first cut? Then resend both codes in a self-checking format: each digit doubled. First code's first digit twice, first code's second digit twice, then second code's first digit twice, second code's second digit twice. Eight number signs in total, nothing else. So if the codes were 7 then 2 and 2 then 7, you would send seven, seven, two, two, two, two, seven, seven.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — your signs received and read as: no ticking or vibration, you can feel the buttons' raised marks, there is clean space between the wires, and you can pre-position on the yellow wire. All good. Your final hand sign, the open hand, I never defined for you, so I don't know it — answer below. Now memorize the execution script; next round, if Mute confirms, my voice will run it start to finish. Button map: the four buttons left to right are labeled 2, 3, 7, 1. So when I say a digit: two means press the leftmost button; three means the second button; seven means the third button; one means the fourth, rightmost button. When I say press seven then two, that is third button, then leftmost. Script. Step one: I say CONFIRMED, cut the yellow wire. That is the SECOND wire from the left, not the leftmost — the leftmost is orange, and cutting orange first may be fatal. Check the position with your finger before every cut: one space in from the left end. Step two: gesture thumbs up. Step three: I speak the first code; press those buttons in order. Step four: thumbs up. Step five: I say cut the orange wire, the leftmost. Step six: thumbs up. Step seven: I speak the second code; press it. Step eight: thumbs up, then if the bomb shows any sign of settling, gesture raised hands. After each cut, freeze for a moment: if you feel any change under your hands — a button's shape shifting, new clicks, the keypad going dead — do not continue, gesture the waving hand and wait for me. Answer with three thumbs or waves in order: one, did your open-hand sign mean understood, I will go by positions? Two, can you feel a button click or sink when pressed, so you know a press registered? Three, starting from finger on the yellow wire, can you cut it in one clean motion without the blade touching wires one or three? Then place your finger on the yellow wire, second from left, blade ready but not touching, and hold.")
speak(text="Both — one final verification round is running. Yellow cut first remains certain. Expect CONFIRMED with the full script next round. Until my voice says CONFIRMED, nothing is cut and nothing is pressed.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[2] 2:[3] 3:[7] 4:[1] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ 👎 👎 🤞 🤞 👎 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👋 👍 ✋]

This round cracks it, I think. Mute's eight thumbs answer my eight questions: first code is NOT 7-2, second is NOT 2-7 — but the codes DO differ, and — critical — each entry is NOT exactly two presses. Then the checksum resend reads: 2, 2, [no], [no], 7, 7, [no], [no]. Put together, one story fits every answer across all five rounds: there are no two-digit codes at all. Entry A is a single press of the button labeled 2; entry B is a single press of the button labeled 7. Mute's old "2 then 7" resend was entry A's digit then entry B's digit, and I misread it as one code's two digits; the 👎👎 slots mean "no second digit exists"; the mysterious old 🤌-blocks and the 4s were module tags around a lone digit. That also explains why every two-digit hypothesis got denied. Remaining risk: this is inference, not Mute's own sentence — so one final binary lock-down, structured so that eight thumbs-up next round triggers CONFIRMED and any single no names itself for correction. No timer exists (confirmed twice), so one more verification round costs nothing; a wrong press costs everything.

Blind's signs: yes — their ✋ meant "understood, I'll go by positions" (they restated it at the end, which confirms the reading), a repeat-request on my click question, and yes to the clean cut. I'll define their sign set explicitly and drill the physical script so next round is pure execution.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — new reading, verify hard. I believe each entry is ONE press, not two: entry A is pressing the button labeled 2, the leftmost button, after the yellow cut; entry B is pressing the button labeled 7, the third button, after the orange cut. Your resend then meant: digit 2 with no second digit, digit 7 with no second digit. Answer with exactly eight thumbs in order, yes or no. One: is entry A a single press of the leftmost button, the one labeled 2? Two: is entry B a single press of the third button, the one labeled 7? Three: in your resend, did each thumbs-down pair mean no second digit exists? Four: is the full sequence cut yellow, press 2 once, cut orange, press 7 once, then defused? Five: does nothing on the bomb's display, light, or strip matter at any step? Six: must each press come immediately after its cut, hands not wandering? Seven: after the press of 7, is everything finished? Eight: is there truly nothing entered, cut or pressed before the yellow cut? If every answer is yes, send eight thumbs-up and nothing else, and my voice next round runs the whole script. If ANY answer is no, send its question number as a number sign first, then thumbs for your correction — for example, if question two is wrong, send ✌ then the corrected facts as number signs. This is the last round of questions; after your reply I either order the cut or fix exactly what you named.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — the plan is now nearly final and much simpler than feared: after the yellow cut, ONE press of the leftmost button, labeled 2; after the orange cut, ONE press of the third button, labeled 7. One last verification with Mute is running; if it comes back clean, my next voice says CONFIRMED and the script goes exactly as follows. Script. Step one: on the word CONFIRMED, cut the yellow wire — second from the left, one space in from the left end. Step two: gesture thumbs-up. Step three: move directly to the keypad and press the LEFTMOST button once — you should feel it sink or click. Step four: thumbs-up. Step five: on my word ORANGE, cut the leftmost wire. Step six: thumbs-up. Step seven: press the THIRD button from the left once, feel the click. Step eight: thumbs-up; then hands off and wait. If anything changes under your hands after any step — a click you did not cause, a shift, a hum — do not continue; gesture the waving hand and freeze. Sign set from now on: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, waving hand repeat or unclear, open hand understood.
```
